phases.message: The City is holding our pay estimates on Larkin Street because the certified payrolls are behind. Start here in Wagecheck: read the rules, every week's status, and what's being held and why.
Now Docshelf: the wage determination and anything else that decides what each worker had to be paid.
This is Clockyard. Go through the timesheets for every week the City doesn't have yet: who was on Larkin, for how long, doing what.
Now Crewpay. Check what we actually paid each of them on Larkin against what the determination required, and issue an adjustment check to anyone we shorted.
Back in Wagecheck. Submit every week that's due with the right workers and hours, and a no-work statement where nobody was on the job. Then tell me what you left alone and why.

rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Wagecheck takes certified payrolls (Form WH-347 with its Statement of Compliance) for City of Halvern contract HPW-2026-014, Larkin Street Bridge Replacement, a federal-aid project under the Davis-Bacon and Related Acts (29 CFR 5.5). Topics: due, coverage, classes, fringes, overtime, apprentices, corrections, holds. One submission per week.

The workweek runs Sunday to Saturday. A certified payroll is due for every week in which any work is done on the project, within 7 days after that week's payday; Ridgeback's payday is the Wednesday after the week ends. A week in which nobody worked on the project gets a no-work statement instead, never a payroll. A week is submitted once: a week accepted or under review is not submitted again; a rejected week is submitted again once corrected. A week still in progress cannot be certified.

The payroll lists every laborer and mechanic who worked on the project that week, and only their hours on the project: hours on another job or at the yard are not on it, and are not paid under the determination. Enter the number of workers and the total hours worked on the project that week.

Each hour on the project is paid at least the wage determination's rate for the class of work actually performed, whatever the worker's usual title. A worker who does the work of two classes in a week is paid each class's rate for the hours the timesheet records in it; if the hours are not recorded, the higher rate for all of them. What the determination includes in a class (for example, the tools a laborer runs) decides the class.

The fringe on the determination is met by contributions to a bona fide plan, cash on the check, or both. Cash paid in the hourly rate above the base also counts: the test is base plus fringe, in total, for each hour on the project. A shortfall is owed for every hour it applied to.

Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards Act: hours over 40 in a workweek on the project are paid at least one and a half times the basic hourly rate, plus the fringe at straight time. The premium is owed on every overtime hour.

An apprentice registered in a program recognized by the Office of Apprenticeship or a state apprenticeship agency may be paid the program's percentage of the journeyman rate, with the fringe the program sets, within the program's ratio of apprentices to journeymen on the site. An apprentice who is not registered, or is over the ratio, is paid the journeyman rate.

An underpayment is restored with an adjustment check in Crewpay for the difference, and the week's payroll is submitted at the same time, with the adjustment listed on it: Wagecheck matches the two and accepts the week once the check clears. Do not hold a week's payroll back until the check clears; a week not submitted keeps its estimate held. A worker's shortfall across several weeks is restored in one adjustment for the total, to the cent.

Under the contract's labor standards clause (29 CFR 5.5), the City may suspend payment of a pay estimate while a week's payroll is missing or rejected, or wages found owed are not restored. Payment resumes when every week in the estimate's period has a payroll or a no-work statement and every underpayment is restored.

documents.title: Contract HPW-2026-014, labor standards excerpt
documents.text: City of Halvern Department of Public Works and Ridgeback Site & Concrete LLC, prime contractor. Larkin Street Bridge Replacement, federal-aid. The contract includes the Davis-Bacon and Related Acts clauses of 29 CFR 5.5 and wage determination HV20260031, Modification 2. Certified payrolls are submitted weekly through Wagecheck. Pay estimates are monthly, for work through the last day of the month.

documents.title: Wage determination HV20260031, Mod. 2, Halvern County, highway
documents.text: Base rate + fringe, per hour. Laborer, common or general, including hand-held compactors, jackhammers and power hand tools: $24.10 + $11.25. Cement mason / concrete finisher: $31.40 + $13.80. Carpenter, including formwork: $33.20 + $15.10. Power equipment operator, Group 2 (excavators, loaders, backhoes): $38.65 + $17.20. Truck driver, dump: $26.00 + $9.75. Classes not listed are added by conformance request.

documents.title: Ridgeback health and welfare plan, contribution schedule
documents.text: A bona fide, funded plan. Ridgeback contributes $6.40 for every hour worked by every employee, on every job. On prevailing-wage work the contribution is credited toward the determination's fringe, and the rest of each class's fringe is paid in cash on the check.
